subtopics.title: Absolute vs Comparative Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Distinguishes absolute evaluation, which measures a model against fixed criteria to determine if it is "good enough" for a specific application, from comparative evaluation, which only ranks models relative to one another.

subtopics.title: Domain-Specific Capability Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Evaluates specialized skills such as code generation, math, and reasoning using domain-specific benchmarks, focusing on functional correctness and exact evaluation methods.

subtopics.title: Generation Capability Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Assesses the quality of generated text using language modeling metrics like perplexity and similarity measurements against reference data when automatic evaluation is possible.

subtopics.title: Instruction-Following Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Measures how well a model adheres to user constraints and guidelines using scoring rubrics, examples, and defined evaluation criteria.

subtopics.title: System-Level Cost and Latency Evaluation
subtopics.summary: Evaluates non-functional requirements such as efficiency, runtime, memory usage, and cost to determine if a model's performance is practical for real-world deployment.

subtopics.title: Evaluation Pipeline Design
subtopics.summary: Outlines the end-to-end process for building an evaluation system, including creating guidelines, defining methods and data, annotating evaluation sets, and iterating based on results.
